KEY MESSAGE 1...Unseasonably mild day behind the storm that has 
already departed the region. Partly-mostly sunny skies developing 
with highs in the middle to upper 60s! A cold front delivers much 
colder temps Tue and Wed with highs only in the 40s...But with dry 
weather.

Fast moving coastal storm has already departed the region! Drier 
westerly flow behind this storm should result in skies becoming 
partly to mostly sunny by lunchtime. 925T still near +11C coupled 
with a warm start should yield high temps in the middle to upper 
60s! Not out of the question a few spots flirt with 70! 

A cold front crosses the region tonight. While it mainly comes 
through dry it will deliver much colder temps to the region for Tue 
into Wed. Cold advection drops 925mb temps from near 11C today to 
-3C Tue-Wed. Despite abundant sunshine this will limit high temps to 
the 40s while good radiational cooling gives us a very cold start to 
Wednesday...lows mainly in the upper teens and 20s. Even the urban 
heat island of Boston should see temps bottom out in the lower 30s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Increasing confidence in an impactful storm 
Thanksgiving into early Fri. Heavy rain, strong winds along the 
coast, dangerous marine conditions, and coastal flooding/beach 
erosion are all potential hazards.

The long term guidance remains in very good agreement in the 
potential for an impactful coastal storm to impact the the region 
Thanksgiving into early Fri. As the prior forecaster mentioned...the 
timing has slowed a bit and think the bulk of the rain will be later 
Thanksgiving day into early Fri. We will break things down more 
below.

Another robust moisture loaded piece of southern stream energy will 
combined with vigorous northern stream energy. This results in an 
intensifying low pressure system lifting northward toward southern 
New England. Unlike a few days ago...the models have trended further 
west with this storm as opposed to a traditional coastal/nor'easter. 
This is a result of the upper level flow becoming highly amplified 
from vigorous northern stream energy. 

This system has the potential to be impactful...particularly along 
the coast for a couple of reasons. The first is that this will be 
associated with a departing 1040 mb high over the Canadian 
Maritimes. This will result in a strong pressure gradient and likely 
result in a period of strong easterly winds along the coast. The 
EPS/NAEFS situational awareness table indicate and easterly LLJ 3-4 
standard deviations outside climatology. This is supportive of 
strong easterly wind gusts...perhaps in the 40-60 mph range along 
the coast. A good bet that we will eventually need some wind 
headlines for this event. 

The biggest concern though right now are the very high astronomical 
tides.  Specifically speaking....Boston has a MLLW of 11.8 feet in 
on Thanksgiving and 11.7 feet on Friday which both occur around 
midday. That is about as high as it gets and that definitely has us 
concerned. At this time...the worst conditions look to occur between 
these two high tides which would be good news. Right now the peak of 
the storm would occur during the lower high tide near 9.9 feet at 
midnight.Its also good news that the track has shifted westward as 
this will limit the duration of the strong easterly wind gusts and 
eventually turn them more southerly. However...if things were to 
slowdown or speedup 4-8 hours...which is still possible in this 
time range...we could be dealing with a very significant coastal 
flood event. However...even if current timing keeps the worst of 
the winds in between high tides...we likely will still have some 
issues given the very high astro tides on both days. Not to mention 
that there also could be issues during the lower high tide near 
midnight if strong winds coincide with that. 

Given the western shift in the track and very limited antecedent 
cold air...Ptype will be a windswept heavy rain. Even across the 
very distant interior...the risk for even a brief period of ice/snow 
was fading. Rainfall should be on the order of 1 to 2"...so not 
thinking any significant flooding issues other than the typical brief 
nuisance poor drainage street flooding. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Mainly dry weather follows this weekend outside
a spot shower with highs mainly in the upper 40s to the middle 
50s with breezy conditions on Saturday.

Low pressure initially over Maine shifts eastward into the Canadian 
Maritimes this weekend. The result will be a drier westerly flow of 
air across the region. While we can not rule out a spot shower or 
two...dry weather should dominate the Holiday Weekend. Highs will 
mainly be in the upper 40s to the middle 50s with a bit of a 
westerly breeze especially on Sat.
